Every checktor check rests on a source, and the source sets its severity. This
page maps each check to its authority, links the exact section wherever one
exists, and gives the severity that authority earns. For the full argument and
the exemptions, read the check's help page, such as `?lab_option_changes`.

## Read the severity

Severity tells you what kind of authority stands behind a check.

- `policy` is a rule CRAN enforces. Breaking one can get a package rejected, and
  a policy finding counts against overall health. Most of these rules are
  written in the [CRAN Repository Policy][policy] or [Writing R
  Extensions][wre], the two documents CRAN treats as binding. Some mirror a CRAN
  incoming check, one of the NOTEs that [`R CMD check --as-cran`][wre-check]
  raises against a submission. For a few long-standing reviewer requirements
  that neither manual states, the [CRAN Cookbook][cookbook] is the written
  record. Restoring `options()`, `par()` and the working directory is
  the clearest case. It is among the most common reasons a package is sent back,
  and neither manual mentions it.
- `robustness` is a real defect that CRAN will still accept, such as a
  `detectCores()` that can return `NA`. It counts toward overall health too,
  because the defect is real whether or not CRAN objects to it.
- `opinion` is a convention that experienced maintainers and reviewers tend to
  ask for, with nothing enforcing it. checktor reports it but leaves it out of
  overall health, which by default counts `policy` and `robustness` alone.

![Three severities side by side. Policy breaks a CRAN rule, such as `set.seed(42)` inside a function. Robustness is a real defect that CRAN still accepts, such as `sorted = F`. Opinion is a convention with no rule behind it, such as a help page with no `\value{}`. Under policy and robustness, a bracket reads Counts toward overall health. Under opinion, a dashed bracket reads Listed, not counted.](figures/severity-light.svg){.ct-fig .ct-light}
![](figures/severity-dark.svg){.ct-fig .ct-dark aria-hidden="true"}

The Source column in each table below gives the authority. Many conventions are
written down in the [CRAN Cookbook][cookbook], the R Contributor guide to the
problems that get packages sent back. Where it has a recipe, the column links to
it. For checks with no citable source, the column reads "No formal rule",
"No rule" or "Convention only".

## Which checks run

Most checks run every time. Some depend on the machine. When one of those
cannot run, `checktor()` reports it as skipped rather than passed,
so good overall health never rests on a check that did not happen. The
`skipped` column of `tidy()` marks it, and `metadata$skipped_checks` lists it.
Checks are also skipped when their input cannot be read. If R cannot read
`DESCRIPTION`, every check that reads its fields is skipped, and
`description_file` reports the problem as a policy finding. If `Authors@R`
cannot be read, `identifier_format` is skipped.

![Three results a check can have. Passed, a green check mark, means it ran and found nothing, as `print_cat_usage` did. Failed, an amber cross, means it ran and found something to fix, as `tf_usage` did. Skipped, a dashed empty ring, means it could not run, as `url_liveness` did, and it never counts as a pass.](figures/check-results-light.svg){.ct-fig .ct-light}
![](figures/check-results-dark.svg){.ct-fig .ct-dark aria-hidden="true"}

Others run only when you call them. Nothing asked for them, so they are not
skipped, and `metadata$on_request_checks` lists them so you can find them.

| Check | Runs | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `url_liveness` | at the console | It fetches every URL, so it stays off in scripts and under `R CMD check`, where the network would decide the result. `options(checktor.url_check = TRUE)` runs it everywhere. |
| `spelling` | with a backend | It needs `aspell` or `hunspell` installed. `options(checktor.spelling = FALSE)` turns it off and reports it as skipped. `options(checktor.disable = "spelling")` or `Config/checktor/disable: spelling` leaves it out of the run entirely. |
| `cran_comments_file` | when you call it | `cran-comments.md` belongs to the submission workflow rather than to the package. |
| `title_starts_with_article` | when you call it | No authority supports it, so it stays available without joining the run. |
| `description_function_quotes` | when you call it | No authority supports it either, and Writing R Extensions points the other way. |
| `cph_role` | when you call it | `?person` says authors who are natural persons hold copyright by default, so most packages need no `cph` role. |
| `format_names` | when you call it | CRAN accepts `JSON`, `HTML`, `SQL` and the other format names written bare, so quoting them is a matter of style. |

Every other check runs always, and new checks join the run unless their row in
the registry says otherwise. No check goes missing because someone forgot to
switch it on.

## Code checks

| Check | Severity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `seed_setting` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: a package "should not modify the global environment", and `set.seed()` writes `.Random.seed` there. Recipe: [Setting a Specific Seed][cb-seed]. |
| `print_cat_usage` | `policy` | [Cookbook: Using print()/cat()][cb-printcat]: diagnostic output belongs in `message()` or `warning()`, which a user can suppress. Reviewers require it, though neither manual states it. |
| `option_changes` | `policy` | [Cookbook: Change of Options, Graphical Parameters and Working Directory][cb-options]: restore anything a function changes, with `on.exit()`. Neither manual states this, but it is among the most common reasons a package is sent back. |
| `warn_option` | `policy` | [Cookbook: Setting options(warn = -1)][cb-warn]: the same requirement, for the warning level. |
| `home_writing` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: "Packages should not write in the user's home filespace ... nor anywhere else on the file system apart from the R session's temporary directory". Recipe: [Writing Files and Directories to the Home Filespace][cb-home]. |
| `globalenv_mod` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: "Packages should not modify the global environment (user's workspace)." Recipe: [Writing to the .GlobalEnv][cb-globalenv]. |
| `installed_packages` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: a package must not install other packages when it runs. Recipe: [Calling installed.packages()][cb-installed]. |
| `software_install` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: a package must not download and install external software at load or run time. Recipe: [Installing Software][cb-software]. |
| `core_usage` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: "If running a package uses multiple threads/cores it must never use more than two simultaneously". Recipe: [Using more than 2 Cores][cb-cores]. |
| `sys_setenv` | `policy` | No clause mentions environment variables, but they are session state in the same way `options()` are, so the same restore-on-exit requirement applies. See [Cookbook: Change of Options, Graphical Parameters and Working Directory][cb-options]. |
| `tf_usage` | `robustness` | No binding rule, but a documented one in [Cookbook: T/F Instead of TRUE/FALSE][cb-tf]. `T` and `F` are ordinary variables (see `?logical`) that code can rebind, so they make unsafe stand-ins. |
| `library_in_pkg` | `robustness` | [WRE: Package Dependencies][wre-deps]: package code should reach dependencies through `Imports` and `::`, not attach them with `library()`. |
| `detect_cores_robustness` | `robustness` | No formal rule. `?detectCores` states it returns "`NA` if the answer is unknown", and the arithmetic that usually follows then crashes. |
| `hardcoded_credentials` | `robustness` | No formal rule. Tokens and keys committed to a package are public the moment it reaches CRAN, and must be revoked. |
| `internal_ns` | `robustness` | CRAN asks you to omit one colon, since `:::` reaches an object whose author may change it. `R CMD check` reports it too, under dependencies in R code. |
| `temp_cleanup` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Leaving Files in the Temporary Directory][cb-temp]. R removes `tempdir()` when the session ends, so a temporary file nobody `unlink()`ed breaks no rule. That keeps this check advisory. |

## DESCRIPTION checks

| Check | Severity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `description_file` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: "Fields start with an ASCII name immediately followed by a colon" and "Continuation lines ... start with a space or tab". `R CMD build` and `R CMD INSTALL` stop on a file that breaks this, or that a blank line splits in two. |
| `description_fields` | `policy` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check]: it NOTEs "Unknown, possibly misspelled, fields in DESCRIPTION", allowing `Config/` and a few other prefixes. `Remotes` is the usual one. [CRAN Policy][policy] wants strong dependencies "available from CRAN or the Bioconductor software repository". |
| `description_placeholders` | `policy` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check]: it NOTEs "DESCRIPTION fields with placeholder content", the `Title`, `Description`, `Author` or `Maintainer` a `usethis` or `package.skeleton()` template wrote. |
| `software_names` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: "Refer to other packages and external software in single quotes". Recipe: [Formatting Software Names][cb-names]. |
| `language_names` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: the same rule, for programming languages and statistical software such as `Python`, `Java`, `MATLAB` and `SAS`. Recipe: [Formatting Software Names][cb-names]. |
| `description_quoted_quotes` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: double quotes are for book titles and similar, and software names take single quotes. The format names `format_names` covers are left out, since CRAN accepts them bare. Recipe: [Formatting Software Names][cb-names]. |
| `license` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: an invalid or unrecognized `License` field is a rejection. Recipe: [LICENSE files][cb-license]. |
| `license_file_unneeded` | `policy` | [Cookbook: LICENSE files][cb-license]: CRAN does "not need" `+ file LICENSE` "and the file as these are part of R", unless the file adds attribution requirements or restrictions. `R CMD check` NOTEs the pointer on a license that takes no extension, and the [incoming check][wre-check] NOTEs it on one that does, such as `GPL-3`. |
| `authors` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: a placeholder or malformed `Authors@R`, including a missing maintainer, is a rejection. Recipe: [Using Authors@R][cb-authors]. |
| `title_case` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: the `Title` "should use title case". The [`--as-cran`][wre-check] incoming check flags one that does not. Recipe: [Title Case][cb-titlecase]. |
| `title_package_name` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: "Do not repeat the package name: it is often used prefixed by the name." The [incoming check][wre-check] NOTEs a `Title` that is the name or starts with it. Only the name alone and `name:` are flagged, since CRAN routinely accepts a name that is an ordinary word, as in "Survival Analysis". |
| `date_format` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: "the 'yyyy-mm-dd' format of the ISO 8601 standard is strongly recommended". The [incoming check][wre-check] also flags a stale or future date. |
| `version_format` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: a `Version` is "a sequence of at least two ... non-negative integers". The [incoming check][wre-check] flags a leading zero or an implausible value. |
| `encoding_utf8` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: a non-ASCII DESCRIPTION "should contain an 'Encoding' field". The [incoming check][wre-check] NOTEs any value other than `UTF-8` as deprecated, `latin1` and `latin2` included. |
| `description_starts_with` | `policy` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: "It is good practice not to start with the package name, 'This package' or similar". The [incoming check][wre-check] flags it. |
| `references` | `policy` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check]: it NOTEs a URL outside `<...>`, a DOI not written `<doi:prefix/suffix>` or given as a publisher link, and an arXiv id where the [submission checklist][checklist] asks for the arXiv DOI `<doi:10.48550/arXiv.ID>`. Recipe: [References][cb-refs]. |
| `identifier_format` | `policy` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check]: it NOTEs a malformed ORCID or ROR identifier in `Authors@R`. |
| `license_year` | `robustness` | No binding rule. Leaving `<YEAR>` or `<COPYRIGHT HOLDER>` in the `LICENSE` template puts a placeholder where the copyright notice belongs. Recipe: [LICENSE files][cb-license]. |
| `spelling` | `opinion` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check] (aspell), but it needs a spell-check backend and is noisy, so checktor keeps it advisory. |
| `acronyms` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Explaining Acronyms][cb-acronyms]. Reviewers ask for an acronym to be spelled out once, but nothing enforces it. |
| `cph_role` | `opinion` | `?person`: `cph` is for copyright holders, and authors who are natural persons hold copyright by default without it. CRAN Policy asks only that ownership be clear, which a `Copyright` field also achieves. Runs on request. |
| `format_names` | `opinion` | No rule. [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc] asks for quotes around software, and `JSON`, `HTML`, `XML`, `CSS`, `YAML`, `TOML`, `Markdown`, `LaTeX`, `TeX` and `SQL` are formats. `C++`, `Fortran` and `Tcl` are written either way. In a census of CRAN in September 2026, packages accepted at new-package review in the previous 18 months wrote these bare 62% of the time, against 28% for the names `language_names` checks. Runs on request. |
| `description_length` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Description Length][cb-desclen]. Reviewers find a one-line `Description` thin and ask for more. |
| `title_length` | `opinion` | [WRE: The DESCRIPTION file][wre-desc]: "Some package listings may truncate the title to 65 characters". That is a display width rather than a limit, so a `Title` that fills it exactly still shows in full, and nothing rejects a longer one. |
| `title_redundant_phrases` | `opinion` | Convention only. Phrases like "R package to" are redundant in a `Title`. |
| `title_starts_with_article` | `opinion` | No rule. The real CRAN rule, which `description_starts_with` enforces, concerns the opening of the `Description`. Kept callable but off by default. |
| `description_function_quotes` | `opinion` | No rule, and Writing R Extensions points the other way. Kept callable but off by default. |

## Documentation checks

| Check | Severity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `suggested_in_examples` | `policy` | [WRE: Suggested packages][wre-sugg]: a package from `Suggests` used in an example must be guarded so the example still runs without it. |
| `rd_bibliography` | `policy` | [WRE: Bibliographic citations and references][wre-bib]: R 4.6's `\bibcitet{}`, `\bibcitep{}` and `\bibshow{}` read the package bibliography. `R CMD check` warns "Could not find bibentries for the following keys" and notes "Bibentries cited but not shown", and `--as-cran` notes a `REFERENCES` file at the top level as non-standard. |
| `roxygen_usage` | `robustness` | No binding rule. Functions tagged `@export` that never reached `NAMESPACE` are not exported. Recipe: [Repeated Rejections of Issues in Manuals If Using roxygen2][cb-roxygen]. |
| `unexported_example_ns` | `robustness` | No formal rule. Examples that reach for an unexported object error when they run. |
| `rd_bibliography_files` | `robustness` | [WRE: Bibliographic citations and references][wre-bib] keeps the bibliography as `inst/REFERENCES.R` or `inst/REFERENCES.bib`, which "needs bibtex to be installed". Nothing checks either. Without `bibtex` in `Suggests`, a `.bib` fails a build that installs only what is declared, and one outside `inst/` is never installed for another package's `pkg::key`. |
| `value_tags` | `opinion` | [WRE: Documenting functions][wre-doc] describes `\value{}`, and [Cookbook: Missing \value-tags in .Rd-files][cb-value] is the recipe reviewers cite, but `R CMD check` does not require it. |
| `example_structure` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Structuring of Examples][cb-examples]. `\dontrun{}` should wrap only code that cannot run inside a check. |
| `donttest_vs_dontrun` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Structuring of Examples][cb-examples]: `\donttest{}` is the wrapper for examples that merely run long, where many reach for `\dontrun{}` instead. |
| `missing_examples` | `opinion` | [Cookbook: Structuring of Examples][cb-examples]. Exported functions are expected to carry an `\examples{}` block. |
| `commented_examples` | `opinion` | Convention only. Commenting out a whole `\examples{}` block leaves it demonstrating nothing. |

## Example, vignette and demo checks

These checks cover the code outside `R/` that CRAN reads, where several of the
most common rejections land. Maintainers have received each rule below,
verbatim, in a reply from CRAN.

![Four folders of a package: `R/` for package code, `man/` for help page examples, `vignettes/` and `demo/`. One green line spans all four and reads checktor reads all four. Under each folder is a finding checktor catches there: a seed set inside a function, an install, a write outside `tempdir()` and `options()` changed for good.](figures/where-checks-read-light.svg){.ct-fig .ct-light}
![](figures/where-checks-read-dark.svg){.ct-fig .ct-dark aria-hidden="true"}

| Check | Severity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `example_interactive` | `policy` | [Cookbook: Structuring of Examples][cb-examples]: a function that only runs interactively belongs in `if (interactive())`, so a reader sees it is not for a script, rather than in `\dontrun{}`. In `\donttest{}` it does more harm, because `R CMD check --as-cran` runs that code, where a prompt errors and an app waits for input. |
| `example_installs` | `policy` | [Cookbook: Installing Software][cb-software]: do not install packages from a function, an example or a vignette. |
| `example_writes` | `policy` | [Cookbook: Writing Files and Directories to the Home Filespace][cb-home]: an example, vignette or test may write only to `tempdir()`. |
| `example_state` | `policy` | [Cookbook: Change of Options, Graphical Parameters and Working Directory][cb-options]: restore `options()`, `par()` and the working directory changed in an example, vignette or demo. |
| `example_internal_ns` | `policy` | CRAN asks you to omit one colon, since `:::` reaches an object whose behavior the author may change. |
| `example_tf_usage` | `robustness` | [Cookbook: T/F Instead of TRUE/FALSE][cb-tf]: `T` and `F` "should not be used as variable names in your code, examples, tests or vignettes". The same rule as `tf_usage`, applied to examples, vignettes and demos. |
| `example_unparseable` | `robustness` | Reviewers send this rejection verbatim: "Unexecutable code in man/...Rd". [WRE: Documenting functions][wre-doc] lets `\dontrun{}` text be something other than R, but reviewers run examples with it included, and `R CMD check` never parses it, so a missing bracket or a `<your key>` placeholder there goes unseen. |

## General checks

| Check | Severity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `code_exercised` | `policy` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check]: `--as-cran` WARNs "No examples, no tests, no vignettes" for a package that exports code and includes none of the three. [CRAN Policy][policy] asks that "the checks that are left do exercise all the features of the package". |
| `citation_file` | `policy` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check]: `--as-cran` NOTEs an `inst/CITATION` that calls the old-style `citEntry()` or `personList()`, and lists calls to `packageDescription()`, `library()` and `require()`. [WRE: CITATION files][wre-citation]: "It is desirable (and essential for CRAN) that the CITATION file does not contain calls to functions such as packageDescription which assume the package is installed". |
| `package_size` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: CRAN limits the size of the built tarball. Recipe: [Package Size][cb-size], which gives the practical figures. |
| `url_liveness` | `robustness` | [CRAN incoming check][wre-check]: `--as-cran` fetches URLs and NOTEs 404s and redirects. It runs at the console and stays off in scripts and checks, where the network would decide the result. |
| `readme_links` | `robustness` | No formal rule. Relative README links whose targets are excluded from the tarball break on the package page. |
| `urls` | `opinion` | Convention only. Preferring `https://` is good advice, but CRAN's NOTE is about broken URLs rather than the scheme. |
| `news_file` | `opinion` | Convention only. `NEWS` files are expected but not required. |
| `cran_comments_file` | `opinion` | Convention only. `cran-comments.md` belongs to the submission workflow rather than to the package, so this check runs only when you call it. |

## CRAN policy checks

| Check | Severity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `browser_calls` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: checks run non-interactively, so a debugging leftover such as `browser()` must not remain. |
| `file_operations` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: "Packages should not write ... anywhere ... apart from the R session's temporary directory". Recipe: [Writing Files and Directories to the Home Filespace][cb-home]. |
| `network_operations` | `policy` | [CRAN Policy][policy]: "Packages which use Internet resources should fail gracefully with an informative message if the resource is not available". |
| `system_calls` | `robustness` | No flat rule. Raw `system()` and `system2()` calls need review for portability, so they are not automatic violations. |

## Leave two recipes to people

checktor has a check for every [CRAN Cookbook][cookbook] recipe that describes a
pattern in your sources. The two recipes without one describe things that no
reading of the sources can settle.

*Overall Checktime* concerns a measurement. The NOTE reads
"Overall checktime 20 min > 10 min", and nothing in your sources tells how long
they will take to run. `R CMD check` reports the figure, and the fix is fewer or
smaller examples, vignettes and tests.

*Communicating with CRAN* is advice on writing to CRAN, including copying
`cran-submissions@r-project.org` and explaining yourself in `cran-comments.md`.
Its one checkable part, whether that file exists, is `cran_comments_file`.

## Resolve a disagreement

Severity records where a check's authority sits, not how strongly checktor
feels about it. Several checks are `opinion` because no authority backs them in
either direction. Of those, `title_starts_with_article`,
`description_function_quotes` and `format_names` stay callable but are left out
of the default run for that reason. `cph_role` stays out because its own source
says most authors need no `cph` role. `cran_comments_file` stays out because it
asks about a submission workflow rather than the package.

If a finding contradicts your reading of the policy, look at its severity first.
Opinion findings open a conversation and require nothing. To turn a check
off for one package, list it in `Config/checktor/disable` in that package's
DESCRIPTION. To turn it off for every package, set `options(checktor.disable =
...)`, for example in `.Rprofile`. Either way, the check does not run at all.
